items.q: Design a payment/money-transfer system that guarantees correctness.
items.a: **Requirements:** transfer money between wallets, no double-charging, no money created or lost, full audit trail, tolerate PSP failures. NFR: strong consistency for the ledger, high availability. **Components:** - API Gateway + Idempotency layer - [[b:Payment Orchestrator]] (Saga: debit→PSP→credit; state PENDING/SUCCESS/FAILED/REVERSED) - [[b:Ledger Service]] (source of truth, double-entry append-only, ACID) - [[b:PSP Adapter]] (circuit breaker + retry + idempotency, handles unknown state) - Outbox + Broker (publishes events) - [[b:Reconciliation]] (settlement reconciliation) **Consistency:** - both legs of an entry inside the same ledger transaction (ACID) - cross-service calls use Saga + Outbox + idempotency - balance reads go to primary, [[r:never cached for decision-making]] :::tip Key takeaway 'Ledger is CP and immutable; external communication is at-least-once so consumers must be idempotent; reconciliation is the final safety net.' That trio is the senior fintech answer. ::: :::deep Invariants when presenting an OTA booking: - [[g:seat/inventory]] is finite and needs anti-double-booking → a hold with a TTL, reconfirmed at issue time - [[g:money]] = ACID double-entry ledger + idempotency - [[g:GDS/PSP integration]] = an untrusted boundary → idempotency + status query + reconciliation - [[g:price & availability]] go stale easily → short-TTL cache, reconfirmed at the final step Saga: hold seat → charge → issue ticket (PNR), compensation is refund/void; the issue step comes last (hardest to undo). Bonus points: overbooking policy, fare rules, idempotent retry when the GDS is flaky. - The LLD round asks something quite different from this one: same prompt, but graded on classes, interfaces, and thread-safety instead of boxes and arrows (22-low-level-design-ood.the-lld-framework-classic-problems.q1). :::

**Requirements:** multi-channel, highly reliable, no spam (dedup + per-user rate limit), respects user preferences, tracks delivery status. Mostly async.

**Flow:**
producer → queue ingestion → router (by type & preference) → per-channel queue → per-channel worker pool → provider adapter (retry + circuit breaker) → DLQ → tracking store.

Also needed: template service + i18n, dedup key, [[g:priority queue]] (OTP > marketing), fan-out + backpressure, status webhook.

:::tip Trade-off
Prioritize reliability and throughput over absolute latency; OTP goes through a priority lane with a tighter SLA.
:::

:::deep
- separate [[b:ingestion]] (accepts requests, fast, async) from [[b:delivery]] (per-channel workers)
- router by type + user preference + quiet hours; provider adapter has provider failover
- dedup key prevents duplicate sends; priority queue (OTP/transactional > marketing); per-user rate-limit against spam; status webhook (delivered/bounced)

OTA: 'e-ticket/booking confirmation' is [[g:transactional]] (must-deliver, aggressive retry, DLQ + alert); marketing is [[o:best-effort]] (droppable under overload — load shedding). Idempotent on (notification_id) avoids double sends on retry.
:::

items.q: Design a URL shortener — what are the key decisions?
items.a:
- generating the short code: [[g:base62 from a sequential ID]] (counter/Snowflake) or hash + collision handling
- store the mapping in a [[b:KV store]] (extremely read-heavy) + hot cache
- redirect 301 (cacheable) / 302 (if click counting is needed)
- [[g:reads ≫ writes]] → cache + read replica

Capacity: 7 base62 characters ≈ 3.5 trillion URLs.

**Quick estimate:** 100M new links/month ≈ 40 writes/sec; reads are roughly 100x that ≈ 4,000 reads/sec → [[g:reads are the real problem]], not writes. Each record is ~500B → ~50GB/month, ~600GB/year: still fits in one KV cluster, so don't design complex sharding before it's needed.

:::deep
- base62 from a sequential ID (counter/Snowflake → encode): unique, no collisions, short; or hash + collision handling (more complex)
- 301 (cached permanently, click counts aren't accurate) vs 302 (click counting/analytics); reads ≫ writes → cache + read replica + CDN
- custom alias (uniqueness check), expiry, async analytics via a queue

[[r:Security pitfalls]]: open redirect (validate the destination domain), sequential guessing (add randomness/hashids if privacy matters). Rate-limit link creation against abuse.
:::

items.q: Design a News Feed / timeline — fan-out on write vs read?
items.a:
Fan-out on write (push)Fan-out on read (pull)
When A postspush into every follower's feed cachedo nothing
Reading the feedO(1), very fastmerge the timeline at read time (expensive)
Write costexpensive (celebrity = millions of writes)cheap
In practice, [[g:hybrid]]: push for regular users, pull for celebrities. Feed cache = a Redis sorted set by time; ranking; keyset pagination. :::deep - [[r:celebrity problem]]: 10M followers = 10M writes on push → pull for celebrities instead (on read, merge the precomputed feed with the celebrity's live fetch) - ranking (chronological vs ML-ranked) changes the architecture; feed consistency is eventual (a few seconds of lag is acceptable) OTA: feeds aren't really needed, but fan-out applies to 'notifying many route-followers about a flight/price change' — push for a small follower count, pull/batch for hot routes. :::

items.q: Design a shared distributed rate limiter service?
items.a:
The service receives (key, limit, window) → returns allow/deny.

- core: token bucket/sliding window on Redis with [[g:atomic Lua]]
- partition by key
- at very large scale: local cache + periodic sync (trading accuracy for latency)
- return 429 + Retry-After; HA for Redis (cluster) + fail-open/closed

:::deep
- core token bucket/sliding-window-counter on Redis via atomic Lua (compute refill and deduct in a single command, avoiding a GET-then-SET race between instances)
- at very large scale: token bucket *local to the edge* (quota = total/N + periodic sync)
- HA: Redis Cluster + replicas; [[b:fail-open]] (APIs, favors availability) vs [[b:fail-closed]] (auth/payment, favors protection)

OTA: shared rate-limiting at the gateway (per B2B partner API key), search (per-IP against scraping bots), protecting the GDS (leaky bucket to stay under quota).

- One Redis call adds ~0.3–1ms to *every* request. At 50k QPS that's 50k commands/sec just to count — that's the point where switching to a local bucket plus periodic sync pays off, not something to build from day one (22.3 has code for both approaches).
:::

Redis [[g:sorted set]] (ZADD/ZRANGE/ZREVRANK) gives O(log n) ranking: instant top-N and a user's rank.

- shard by region/leaderboard
- periodic snapshot to durable storage (a sorted set is in-memory)
- tie-break with a secondary score component (timestamp)
- millions of users → shard by bucket + merge top-N

:::deep
- `ZADD` updates a score, `ZREVRANK` gets a user's rank, `ZREVRANGE` returns top-N instantly (skip list + hash)
- tie-break with a combined score (score×10^k + inverted timestamp); at large scale: shard by bucket/region then merge top-N (scatter-gather)
- an exact rank for the 1-millionth user is expensive if strictly real-time → accept an approximate rank/percentile for the tail, exact for the top

OTA: sorted sets are used for 'hot routes/seat-inventory counts', 'most-searched destinations', sliding-window rate limiting. A ZSET is a general 'ranking + range by score' structure.
:::

- shard with [[g:consistent hashing]]; replication for HA
- eviction (LRU/LFU); TTL
- hot keys (replica/local cache); stampede (single-flight)
- cache↔DB consistency (cache-aside + invalidation)
- track hit ratio; client-side vs proxy-based sharding

:::deep
- consistent hashing (adding/removing a node remaps few keys); replication (primary-replica per shard); eviction (LRU/LFU/allkeys-lru); TTL
- [[r:hot key]]: replicate key#1..N + pick randomly, or a client-side local cache; [[r:stampede]]: single-flight + jittered TTL + refresh-ahead
- cache↔DB consistency: cache-aside + invalidate (delete) on write (not update, to avoid races)
- client-side sharding (smart client) vs proxy-based (twemproxy/Redis Cluster)

Track hit ratio (low → the cache is useless or the key design is wrong); distinguish cache (can be lost) from store (source of truth). OTA: short-TTL price/availability cache + invalidate on GDS events.

- The LLD round asks exactly the core of this system: implementing an LRU cache's get/put in O(1) with a HashMap plus a doubly-linked list (22-low-level-design-ood.the-lld-framework-classic-problems.q2); the version with TTL added is a separate prompt (22-low-level-design-ood.patterns-in-interview-code.q4).
:::

- WebSocket gateway holds connections; messages travel via a queue
- storage (Cassandra keyed by `conversation_id + time` — write-heavy)
- online presence (Redis), delivery/read receipts, fan-out to devices, push when offline
- ordering within a conversation (sequence/partition key), idempotency against duplicates

:::deep
- WebSocket gateway (Netty NIO, many connections/thread); messages via a queue; storage optimized for both writes and reads per conversation (Cassandra `(conversation_id, time)`)
- presence (Redis TTL heartbeat), delivery/read receipts, fan-out to devices, push when offline
- [[g:ordering within a conversation]] (sequence number/partition key by conversation_id) & idempotency (client message id against duplicate sends)

Scaling connections means separating the gateway from business logic + pub/sub (Redis/Kafka) so every gateway node can fan out to clients (see 16.9); a user→node registry handles routing. Large group chats use hybrid fan-out like a news feed. E2E encryption changes the architecture (the server can't read message content).
:::

- [[b:Trie/prefix tree]] (or Elasticsearch completion suggester) for prefix-based suggestions
- precompute top-K per node; hot cache
- update frequency counts asynchronously
- extremely low latency → serve from cache/in-memory at the edge
- personalization & ranking by popularity

:::deep
- Trie/prefix tree (or ES completion suggester / FST); *precompute top-K* at each trie node (by popularity) → O(prefix length), very fast
- hot cache + serve in-memory/at the edge (latency < 100ms); update popularity asynchronously (doesn't block reads); personalize by history/geography
- trade-off between freshness and precomputation; fuzzy matching (typos) is more expensive (edit distance/n-gram)

OTA: airport/city autocomplete (a finite set → trie + alias/IATA code + multi-language + prioritize large/nearby airports). A static set → precompute everything + cache; client-side debounce cuts down requests.
:::

items.q: Design object storage / large file uploads (overview)?
items.a:
- object store (S3-like) + metadata DB
- upload directly to the store using a [[g:presigned URL]] (bypassing the app server)
- multipart upload for large files; CDN for reads
- dedup (content hash), async virus scanning, lifecycle/expiry
- [[r:avoid pushing bytes through the service tier]]

:::deep
- object store for bytes + metadata DB for information; client→store upload via a presigned URL (do NOT push bytes through the app server → saves bandwidth/threads)
- multipart upload (chunked, resumable, parallel); CDN for reads; dedup by *content hash*; async: virus scan, transcode, thumbnail via a queue; lifecycle/tiering (hot→cold→archive)
- [[r:security]]: short-TTL presigned URLs + scope; validate content-type/size; guard against path traversal

OTA: passport/visa uploads (sensitive PII → encrypted at rest + access control + audit + compliance-driven retention); e-ticket PDFs live in object storage + CDN.
:::

items.q: Design an Idempotent Payment API (contract details)?
items.a:
`POST /payments` with an `Idempotency-Key` header.

On the server, within one tx:
- INSERT the key (unique) with status IN_PROGRESS
- if a duplicate is still processing → 409/poll; if a duplicate already finished → return the previous result
- perform the business logic + store the response tied to the key
- return 201 + the resource

The key has a reasonable TTL. This is the [[g:'hello world' of safe financial APIs]].

:::deep
- INSERT the key (unique, IN_PROGRESS) in the same tx; store the response tied to the key (or via outbox); return 201 + resource + Location; key TTL scoped by (user, endpoint)
- distinguish [[b:idempotency-key]] (client-supplied, prevents double-submit) from [[b:request-id]] (tracing)

OTA: every outbound call to the PSP carries a key (or order_id) → the PSP is idempotent too → network retries don't double-charge. PSP webhooks are idempotent (unique event_id). Status is PENDING while the PSP hasn't confirmed yet; reconciliation resolves stuck transactions. [[o:A solid grasp of the IN_PROGRESS/race flow is what sets candidates apart.]]
:::
